excerpt: ROME Therapeutics was a biotech developing cancer and autoimmune drugs from the repeatome, the repetitive 'dark' part of the genome. It wound down in 2025 and became a subsidiary of Pretzel Therapeutics in January 2026.
content:
ROME Therapeutics was a biotechnology company that tried to turn the repeatome into medicines. The repeatome is the large share of the human genome, roughly 60% according to the company's 2021 funding announcement, made up of repetitive DNA sequences that were long dismissed as junk. ROME built a platform it called repeatomics to study them, and its lead programme was a LINE-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitor aimed at autoimmune diseases, with cancer as a second focus.

ROME launched in 2020 with $50 million of Series A funding and in September 2021 raised a $77 million Series B led by Section 32, with Sanofi Ventures, Casdin Capital, Andreessen Horowitz and Alexandria Venture Investments joining founding investors ARCH Ventures, GV and Mass General Brigham Ventures. Endpoints News reported a further $72 million extension backed by Johnson & Johnson and Bristol Myers Squibb, taking the Series B to $149 million. Rosana Kapeller was CEO; the scientific co-founders included David Ting of Massachusetts General Hospital Cancer Center and Benjamin Greenbaum of Memorial Sloan Kettering.

Wound down and acquired. In September 2025 Fierce Biotech reported that ROME planned layoffs, was reviewing strategic options and would move to a fully virtual model, citing challenging market conditions. In January 2026 Fierce Biotech reported that ROME had finished winding down its operations and would operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Pretzel Therapeutics, a mitochondrial-medicine company whose CEO and COO had both previously worked at ROME, with ROME's scientific co-founders continuing to advise. Terms were not disclosed. ROME's old website no longer loads.

ROME never had an approved product, so there is nothing to buy or price. This profile draws on published reporting and company announcements. It is not medical advice, and nothing here is paid placement.
